text: Got it — investigating the `Interval.fromISO` / `Settings.throwOnInvalid` bug in src/interval.js now.
Acknowledged — also looking into the `src/impl/util.js` bug affecting `DateTime#plus` across the 100 barrier through February.
Acknowledged — also looking into the `src/datetime.js` bug affecting `DateTime#isInDST()` for the 1974 US year-round DST period.
Acknowledged — also looking into the `src/duration.js` bug affecting `Duration#normalize` unit-pair conversions.

Fixed #1 (src/interval.js). Root cause: `Interval.fromISO` called `DateTime.fromISO` on both halves; with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` those calls throw `InvalidDateTimeError` instead of letting the code fall through to the `Duration.fromISO` fallback / `Interval.invalid(...)` path, so valid duration-form intervals threw and invalid input threw the wrong error type. Now each half's parse is guarded, so `throwOnInvalid` yields `InvalidIntervalError` for unparsable input and valid duration-form intervals parse normally. Verified: Interval suite 127/127 pass; only pre-existing unrelated failures (2 French-locale `toFormat` tests) remain.
Acknowledged — also looking into the `src/impl/util.js` bug affecting negative-year padding in `DateTime#toISODate()`.

Fixed #2 (src/impl/util.js). Root cause: `objToLocalTS` built the timestamp with `Date.UTC(...)` (which maps years 0–99 to 19XX) and then subtracted 1900 from the resulting year. When the passed calendar object is unnormalized (as `DateTime#plus` does, e.g. `{year: 99, month: 12, day: 92}`), the day overflow was computed in 1999/2000 — and 2000 is a leap year while 100 is not — so crossing Feb 29 of year 100 landed one day early. Fix: re-apply `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` so the overflow is recomputed in the correct target year. Verified: full suite unchanged (2 pre-existing unrelated French-locale toFormat failures), plus a brute-force differential check against an exact civil-calendar reference for years 90–110 × every month/day × ±400 days → 0 mismatches (was ~39k before).
Acknowledged — also looking into the `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` bug (non-numeric offset should yield an invalid zone / invalid DateTime).

Fixed #5 (src/impl/util.js). Root cause: `padStart(input, n)` padded the whole string including the minus sign, so `-5` with n=4 gave `"00-5"` and `-100` got no padding at all. Fix: emit the sign separately and zero-pad the digits (`-5` → `-0005`, `-100` → `-0100`), matching `Intl.NumberFormat` minimumIntegerDigits. Positive years unchanged. Verified: full suite identical to baseline (only the 2 pre-existing unrelated French-locale toFormat failures); format tests 59/59 pass; ad-hoc checks for `toISODate`/`toISO`/`toISOWeekDate`/`toFormat` all pass.

Fixed #4 (src/duration.js). Root cause: incomplete conversion matrices — `casualMatrix.years` lacked `quarters`, `casualMatrix.quarters` lacked `seconds`, and `accurateMatrix.years` lacked `quarters`. A missing entry made `convert()` return `undefined` → `NaN`, silently coerced to 0 by the value getters. So `years↔quarters` and `quarters↔seconds` were broken (`{years:1}.as('quarters')` gave 0 instead of 4, `{quarters:1}.as('seconds')` gave 0 instead of 7862400, `shiftTo` gave NaN). Added the three documented factors (1y=4q, 1q=91d=91*24*3600s). Verified: duration suite 114/114 pass; full suite identical to baseline (only the 2 pre-existing unrelated French-locale toFormat failures); an all-9×9-unit-pair ad-hoc check that failed on exactly those 4 pairs before now passes, and a 20k-case fuzz shows the change is strictly additive.

Fixed #3 (src/datetime.js). Root cause: `isInDST` compared the current offset against `this.set({ month: 1 })`, which keeps the day-of-month, so the "standard time" reference was the same day in January rather than Jan 1. In 1974 (US year-round DST, Jan 6–Oct 27) any date with day ≥ 6 had both reference points inside DST, so `isInDST` wrongly returned false (249 wrong days in New York, 320 in Los Angeles). Fix: anchor the reference at `{ month: 1, day: 1 }`. Verified: full suite identical to baseline (only the 2 pre-existing unrelated French-locale toFormat failures); zone/DST suites pass; a full 1974 sweep across 14 zones against an independent reference shows 0 mismatches.
